conventions.convention: The dimensionless torus is R³/(2πZ)³; the physical torus is R³/(2πLZ)³. Fields use periodic lifts, and spatial integrals are unnormalized Riemann integrals over the respective fundamental cubes.
Use x=Ly, t=(L/U)s, u=Uv, varphi=Phi_* phi, and p=rho_* U² pi, with strictly positive scales. The physical chemical potential is mu=(rho_* U²/Phi_*)mu_c.
The velocity gradient has entries ∂_j u_i, tensor divergence has components sum_j ∂_j sigma_ij, and traction is sigma n. The adopted capillary stress has divergence −varphi grad(mu).

The phase variable is an internal scalar order parameter, not total mass density; no positivity or pointwise interval constraint is imposed. Mobility, viscosity, and density are constant and positive.

The smooth branch requires v in C¹(time;C²_per), phi in C¹(time;C¹_per) intersect C(time;C²_per), pi in C(time;C¹_per), and the defined mu_c in C(time;C²_per). The energy identity concerns interior times and kinetic plus phase free energy, not complete thermodynamic energy.

load_bearing.statement: Adopt the smooth periodic, constant-density incompressible equations ∂_t varphi+u·grad(varphi)=Mcal Δmu, div(u)=0, and rho_*(∂_t u+(u·grad)u)=div(sigma), with mu=f_b'(varphi)−lambda_phi Δvarphi and the explicitly displayed viscous and capillary stress. No external body force, interval constraint, empirical calibration, or thermal completion is adopted.

For positive L,U,rho_*,Phi_* and dimensionless epsilon,M,nu>0, define beta=rho_*U²/epsilon, lambda_phi=rho_*U²L²epsilon/Phi_*², eta=rho_*ULnu, and Mcal=M Phi_*²L/(rho_*U), with the stated scale map, chemical potential, and kinetic-plus-phase free-energy functional.

Under its stated positive-parameter, W∈C²(R) bounded-below, periodic regularity, and adopted-equation hypotheses, dG/dt=−eta integral |grad_x u|² dx−Mcal integral |grad_x mu|² dx for 0<t<T_*S. This neither asserts solution existence nor derives the isothermal closure from total-energy or entropy balance.

published_dependencies.used_for: The mathematical energy supplier uses the real mean value theorem to control potential-energy difference quotients; the periodic integration-by-parts supplier uses it on coordinate segments.
The mathematical energy supplier uses compactness of a closed bounded interval to establish boundedness and uniform continuity of W' on the local phase range.
